history.dynasty: Legendary (Banasura) / Salasthamba; present structure early 20th century
history.period: Legend: Puranic age; stone temple 8th-10th century CE (archaeologists' dating); present structure early 20th century
history.summary: CSV town 'Sonitpur' is the district, not the town - corrected to Tezpur. Legend says demon king Banasura, whose capital was at Tezpur, introduced linga worship here and set up the Shiva linga inside, said to be one of the largest stone Shiva lingas in the world. Archaeologists date the original stone temple to the 8th-10th century CE under Salasthamba kings; huge stone pillars scattered around attest to it. The original temple was destroyed by time and later invasions, rebuilt repeatedly, and heavily damaged by the 1897 earthquake; the present structure was built in the early 20th century by the devotee-ascetic Sri Swayambar Bharati (Naga Baba). Idols of Ganesha and Hanuman stand as dvarpalas at the gateway. Opening hours conflict across sources: 6:00 AM-8:00 PM (Incredible India, AartiGyan) vs 6:00 AM-10:00 PM (Justdial) - verify on visit.

name: Mahabhairab Temple
town_description: Tezpur, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra in Sonitpur district, is often called the cultural capital of Assam for its traditions of music, drama and the arts. Ancient as Sonitpur - the 'city of blood' of Banasura legend - it mixes mythic sites (Agnigarh, Bamuni Hills) with colonial-era institutions and parks.

travel.railway: Dekargaon Railway Station, about 10 km away
travel.road: Atop a hillock in the northern part of Tezpur town, reachable by road; Tezpur is connected to Guwahati by NH-27

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri (February/March) is the busiest festival period
